description: Celestial Pioneers 🚀 is participating in the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Trivandrum. Our challenge explores equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars through research, technology, and creative storytelling. We welcome curious minds passionate about space, coding, design, and innovation. Let's learn, collaborate, and bring forgotten space stories to life! 🌌
summary: SPACE LORE is an interactive storytelling website that brings back the stories of objects abandoned on the Moon and Mars, in line with the theme “Abandoned, But Not Forgotten.” We chose 10 relics, five from each world: Apollo 11 Descent Stage, Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package , Lunar Laser Ranging Retroreflector and Surveyor 3 on the Moon, and Mars Pathfinder Lander, Sojourner Rover , Spirit Rover , Opportunity Rover  and Ingenuity Mars Helicopter on Mars. Visitors start on a landing page, choose the Moon or Mars, pick a relic and tap “Discover Its Story” to read how it was built, launched, what it achieved, why it was left behind, where it is now and its legacy. Each story has a “Did You Know?” section, Previous/Next relic navigation, NASA sources and image credits. SPACE LORE makes space history accessible and shows that exploration leaves more behind than footprints.
details:
SPACE LORE is a website that tells the stories of 10 abandoned objects, five on the Moon and five on Mars, so people can learn their history and legacy in an engaging way.

How it works: The user opens the landing page and selects Explore. They choose the Moon (“The Silent Witness”) or Mars (“The Red Frontier”) and see the five relics for that world. Tapping “Discover Its Story” opens a full story in eight chapters: the opening hook, meet the relic, why it was created, its journey into space, its greatest achievement, the moment it was left behind, where it is now, and its legacy. A “Did You Know?” section adds extra facts. At the end of every story, users can go to the previous or next relic, and each story lists its NASA sources and image credits.

Benefits and impact: Most people know the famous missions but not the machines still on the Moon and Mars. SPACE LORE makes this history easy to read and helps people see the value of the missions that came before.

Tools and technologies: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, written in Visual Studio Code and previewed with Live Server.

Creativity: We told each object’s story as a short narrative instead of a list of facts, in a dark, space-style design with animated stars.

Factors we considered: Accuracy and credit. Facts come from NASA sources, the stories are written in our own words, and every story lists its sources and image credits.

Use of Super Intelligence: We used Claude (Anthropic) for early ideas and brainstorming. We used ChatGPT (OpenAI) for website structure, code improvements, debugging and UI suggestions. All research and NASA facts were checked against NASA sources by our team.
